clue.text: Pound family rejected Bohemian Fifties poet

indicators.note: what is rejected is turned back, so these letters are sent the other way

blocks.note: to pound is to beat
kin are your family

explanation.surface: Ezra Pound's relatives disowning some bohemian poet of the 1950s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like the poet Ezra Pound, which suits the literary surface, but it is a verb meaning beat.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beat Generation writers of the 1950s, such as Ginsberg and Kerouac, were nicknamed after this word, and the word came to mean any bohemian.

clue.text: Bad debt I’m last to settle, now I’m ready for the sack

definitions.text: now I’m ready for the sack

indicators.note: something bad has gone wrong, so these letters come out in the wrong order
the last of a word is its final letter, so only that letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A debtor promising to pay up at last, while someone else is about to be fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The sack' sounds like being dismissed from a job, but here it is slang for bed. The anagram of DEBT IM gives BEDTIM, and the E from settle completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitting the sack is slang for going to bed, so the moment you are ready for it is the hour you retire for the night.

clue.text: Adult assumed attitude upset fabulous writer

indicators.note: to upset is to overturn, and in a down clue an overturned word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
a pose is an attitude struck for effect

explanation.surface: A grown-up striking a pose that annoys a wonderful author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' looks like praise, but it means a writer of fables.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek storyteller is famous for his fables, so he is literally a writer of fables, a fabulous writer.

clue.text: S African resident having place erected in North America

indicators.note: something erected is put upright, and in a down clue that means reading upward
one thing set in another sits inside it

blocks.note: to lay something is to place it
NA is the abbreviation for North America

explanation.surface: A South African who has had a house built in the United States or Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resident' suggests a person, but this one is an animal native to the region.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a spiral-horned antelope native to southern Africa, so it lives there as a resident of the region.

clue.text: Sauce boat carried by uniform page

indicators.note: in a down clue what is carried sits on top of its bearer, so one piece comes above the others

blocks.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
Uniform is the radio alphabet word for U
P is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: A gravy boat brought to the table by a page boy in livery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce boat' reads as one kitchen item, but the definition stops after the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomato-based condiment is a common table sauce, the best known example of the type.

clue.text: Cover western hip-hopper

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for western
a performer of hip-hop music raps

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' looks like a cover version of a song, which suits the hip-hop surface, but it means a protective outer layer.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper or film around a sweet or parcel is a protective outer layer, which is what a cover is.

clue.text: Pensive husband leaves card game almost drunk

indicators.note: whoever leaves is no longer present, so that letter is dropped
almost means not quite all, so the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
whist is a trick-taking card game; the H goes from it
full is slang for drunk; its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A thoughtful man walks out of a card game when he is nearly drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: WHIST loses its H, and FULL loses its last L.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a quiet, thoughtful mood, often tinged with longing or regret, so they are close synonyms.

clue.text: Chief detective probing technology design expert

indicators.note: a probe goes into something, so one piece is pushed inside another

blocks.note: arch means chief, as in archbishop
IT stands for information technology
tec is short for detective

explanation.surface: A senior police detective investigating a technology firm's designer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chief detective' reads as one rank, but chief and detective are separate pieces. Tec is old slang for a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: This professional designs buildings and plans their construction, so is an expert in design.

clue.text: Excited his Topic contains a nut

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up, so these letters are jumbled
what contains something holds it inside

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's lively discussion topic includes a nut, as though it were a crank.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters PISTCHIO hold the A after the fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This green kernel from a Middle Eastern tree is a well known edible nut, so it is an example of the category.

clue.text: Refreshed order to include mobile network browser

indicators.note: a refreshed thing is made over anew, so these letters are rearranged
to include something is to take it inside

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
EE is a British mobile phone network

explanation.surface: A web page reloads its ordering to cope with a phone network's browser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Browser' suggests a web browser, but it means an animal that browses, feeding on shoots and leaves. EE is slipped in before the final R.
explanation.definitionFit: These small European deer feed by nibbling shoots and leaves from shrubs, which is called browsing, so they are browsers.

clue.text: Cerebral Frenchman taking part in Mercedes car test

indicators.note: what takes part in something is a portion of it, so the answer is a run of letters inside the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A clever Frenchman taking part in a road test of a German luxury car.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the end of Mercedes through car into test.
explanation.definitionFit: The seventeenth-century French philosopher who wrote 'I think, therefore I am' is the archetype of the cerebral thinker.

clue.text: Ms Blanchett touring second class

indicators.note: to tour is to go all around a place, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: Cate Blanchett is the Australian actress
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: The actress Cate Blanchett is on tour and travelling second class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second class' reads as a travel ticket, but second is a piece and class alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hereditary social rank, especially in the Hindu system, is a rigid social class.

clue.text: What UK constituencies have to call into question?

blocks.note: first meaning, read cryptically: one MP each, with the Roman numeral I for one
second meaning: to challenge or cast doubt upon

explanation.walkthrough: Every UK constituency elects one Member of Parliament, so the answer splits as I MP EACH.
explanation.definitionFit: To challenge the honesty or validity of something, such as a witness's testimony, is to cast doubt upon it formally.

clue.text: Armed HMS Destiny loaded with equipment

indicators.note: something loaded with cargo has it inside, so one piece is packed into another

blocks.note: fate is destiny
rig is equipment, as in a drilling rig

explanation.surface: A Royal Navy ship called Destiny, armed and stocked with kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'HMS Destiny' looks like a ship's name, but the definition takes Armed HMS and Destiny is a piece. HMS (His Majesty's Ship) prefixes Royal Navy vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a medium-sized warship of the Royal Navy, so an armed vessel bearing the HMS prefix.

clue.text: Spilled Pepsi-Cola belonging to the bishop

indicators.note: a spilled drink is scattered everywhere, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written, hyphen dropped

explanation.surface: A fizzy drink knocked over, and it was the bishop's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spilled' fits the drink in the surface, so it hides its job as the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective comes from the Greek for overseer and describes anything relating to a bishop or governed by bishops.

clue.text: Play where Puck comes in for a bit of stick?

definitions.text: Play where Puck comes in for a bit of stick?

blocks.clueFragment: Play where Puck comes in for a bit of stick?
blocks.note: surface reading: a stage play in which Shakespeare's mischievous sprite Puck gets criticised

blocks.clueFragment: Play where Puck comes in for a bit of stick?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a game in which the small rubber disc is hit with sticks

explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' and 'Puck' summon A Midsummer Night's Dream, and 'stick' as criticism. The capital P is a disguise: a puck is the disc struck in a sport played on a rink.
explanation.definitionFit: In this winter team sport players strike a flat rubber disc with curved sticks, so the disc literally takes some stick.

clue.text: Caught game bird flying around university city

indicators.note: whatever is flying around darts every which way, so these letters are thrown about

blocks.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pheasant caught while it was flapping about over a college town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game bird' reads as the creature being caught, but it is the letters to rearrange. Ambridge is also the village in the radio soap The Archers.
explanation.definitionFit: This English city on the River Cam is home to one of the oldest and most famous universities in the world.

clue.text: Heavens! One or the other, just take one away!

indicators.note: to take something from a word is to remove it, so a letter is removed
away completes the phrase meaning removed, so that letter is gone

blocks.note: either means one or the other
I is the Roman numeral for one, removed

explanation.surface: An exasperated parent told to choose one of two things: just take one!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavens!' looks like an exclamation, but it is the definition. EITHER loses its I.
explanation.definitionFit: In poetic and old scientific usage this word names the clear upper air or the sky above, which is the heavens.

clue.text: Mabel undressed in the morning to the side of a ship

definitions.text: to the side of a ship

indicators.note: undressed means stripped of outer clothing, so the outside letters come off

blocks.note: the name with its first and last letters stripped
am means in the morning, ante meridiem

explanation.surface: Mabel, getting undressed in the morning, wanders over to the side of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undressed' strips a word of its outer letters, so the name loses M and L.
explanation.definitionFit: This nautical adverb means at right angles to the keel, level with the middle of the vessel on one side.

clue.text: As Wenger lacking energy in charge?

indicators.note: what is lacking is missing, so a letter goes

blocks.note: Arsène Wenger was the long-serving Arsenal football manager
E is the symbol for energy, removed
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A question whether a football manager is still in charge now that he has run out of steam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' reads as a small linking word, but it is the chemical symbol and the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: As is the symbol on the periodic table for this poisonous chemical element, number 33.

clue.text: Cocky hobo, sanctimonious, nursing temperature

indicators.note: to nurse is to cradle and hold close, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: a bum is a vagrant, in American usage
pious can mean self-righteously religious
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A smug, self-righteous tramp who is running a fever.
explanation.walkthrough: Bum is American slang for a tramp, and the hobo's piety sounds like praise but is meant as a sneer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone self-assertive and conceited to an irritating degree, so they are near synonyms.

clue.text: Airline’s transporting granny, slightly potty

indicators.note: a carrier transporting passengers has them on board, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: BA is British Airways, plus the S of the possessive
nana is a familiar name for a grandmother

explanation.surface: An airline flying an elderly grandmother who is a bit eccentric.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-S of 'Airline's' supplies a real letter, so the whole piece is BAS.
explanation.definitionFit: To go this way is informal slang for becoming crazy, and potty is British slang for mildly mad.

clue.text: Reportedly encounter Greek character that’s rather crusty

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

blocks.note: to encounter is to meet, and pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Supposedly meeting a Greek person who turns out to be rather grumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crusty' reads as bad-tempered, which suits the character of the surface, but it means having a pastry crust.
explanation.definitionFit: A savoury dish of meat baked inside pastry has a crust all round, so it is something rather crusty.

clue.text: Son cleared out lean-to outbuilding the worse for wear

indicators.note: a room cleared out has had its contents removed, leaving only the shell

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
the hyphenated word with its inside letters emptied
a shed is a simple outbuilding

explanation.surface: A son clearing a run-down shed and lean-to that have seen better days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The worse for wear' seems to describe the shabby shed, but it describes a drunk person.
explanation.definitionFit: This is British slang for drunk, and 'the worse for wear' is a common euphemism for having drunk too much.

clue.text: Introduction to steamy erotica featuring artist in fur-trimmed pouch

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the start, so only the first letter is kept

RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: An artist's racy picture tucked into a furry little bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artist' gives RA for a member of the Royal Academy, a crossword staple. A sporran is worn with a Scottish kilt.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the leather or fur pouch worn hanging at the front of a Scottish kilt, often trimmed with fur.

clue.text: Everybody say “run out!” quickly!

blocks.note: all means everybody
e.g. means for example, as does say
RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: A crowd at a cricket match all appealing for a run-out at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like a verb telling everybody to shout, but it means for example. In cricket a batter is run out when the wicket is broken before they make their ground.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian musical direction tells the player to perform at a brisk, lively speed.

clue.text: Bed topless actor

blocks.note: a player is an actor; its first letter goes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed' suggests sleeping, but here it means a stratum, as in a bed of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed of rock or gravel is a stratum, a flat sheet lying over or under others.

clue.text: Plot good knock, opening for Hampshire

indicators.note: an opening is a beginning, so only the first letter is taken

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a rap is a sharp knock
the first letter of the county

explanation.surface: A cricket report: a good innings by the opening batter for Hampshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock' and 'opening' suggest cricket, where a knock is an innings, but knock means rap. Hampshire is an English county with a cricket team.
explanation.definitionFit: To plot points on axes is to draw a chart, and the noun for such a chart is a diagram of data.

clue.text: Bare necessities as kids eat dad’s starters

blocks.note: the initial letters of the five words

clue.text: New York admits program over-hasty, a wee problem

indicators.note: to admit someone is to let them in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York
an app is a software program
rash means acting too hastily

explanation.surface: A rushed computer program launched in New York has a small bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A wee problem' sounds like a minor one, but wee also means urine. A nappy is the British word for a diaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Babies get this sore red skin from wet diapers, so it is literally a problem caused by wee.

clue.text: Yes, Cons affected a certain modesty …

indicators.note: something affected has been altered, so these letters are changed in order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Conservatives putting on a show of modest agreement.

explanation.definitionFit: This means a shy or bashful reluctance, often put on, which is a particular kind of modesty.

clue.text: … insulated against shocks, somewhat near the Democrats

indicators.note: somewhat means to some extent, so only part of the words is used

blocks.note: the letters run from the first word to the start of the third

explanation.surface: Continuing the political theme: a party protected from scandals by sitting close to the Democrats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocks' suggests political upsets, but it means electric shocks. Earthed is the British term for grounded.
explanation.definitionFit: An appliance connected to the ground by a wire is protected so that faults do not give users an electric shock.
